purpose: Adds a 'Load Block Assets On Demand' toggle integrating WP 6.8's should_load_block_assets_on_demand filter to load block CSS/JS only when blocks are present.
riskRationale: The has_filter() version guard on line 437 is incorrect — it checks for registered callbacks rather than filter existence, which means the feature silently does nothing on WP 6.8 when no prior callback exists (which is always the case during plugin bootstrap). This breaks the entire feature.

text: The JS and PHP default/state wiring is clean and follows existing patterns. However, the core PHP side has a critical logic bug: `has_filter()` does not check whether a filter exists — it checks whether any callbacks are already attached. Since `setup_hooks()` runs during plugin bootstrap before any other code has hooked into `should_load_block_assets_on_demand`, the condition always evaluates to `false`, and the `add_filter()` call is never reached. This renders the entire feature inoperative on WP 6.8.

reasoning: The has_filter() guard on line 437 of class-main.php prevents the add_filter() from ever executing on WP 6.8, making the entire feature dead code. Remove the has_filter() check to fix.

message: Default state 'blockAssetsOnDemand: false' is correctly placed in the defaultSettings object following the pattern of the other core bloat toggles.
SwitchField for block assets on-demand is cleanly positioned after disableXMLRPC in the Core sub-tab, following the existing UI pattern and using proper translated strings.
Default option 'blockAssetsOnDemand' => false is correctly added following the same pattern as other file_optimisation booleans.

has_filter() does not check if a filter exists in WP core — it checks if any callbacks are already registered on that hook. Since setup_hooks() runs during plugin bootstrap (from the constructor at line 202, called on line 44 of the main plugin file), no other code has had a chance to hook into 'should_load_block_assets_on_demand' yet, so has_filter() always returns false even on WP 6.8. The add_filter() inside the condition is never reached, making the entire feature dead code.
suggestion: Remove the has_filter() guard entirely. On WP < 6.8, apply_filters('should_load_block_assets_on_demand') is never called, so the add_filter() is a harmless no-op — the callback is stored but never invoked. On WP >= 6.8, the filter fires correctly.
